sentences.sentence: I woke up as a different person today.
I am an altogether different person this year.
But I still feel like the 13 year old me is watching me over.
I remember how she never wanted to grow up, thinking she would lose her innocence, her naivete, her fun and her friends as she grew older.
Today, on my daughter's birthday, I was flooded with such memories.
But instead of remembering the 13 year old, I remembered the 6 year old.
I remembered when she had only just started school, how eager to go there every day for her first few months.
How we'd talk about her day, and the first time I realized that her day meant more than mine.
This is my daughter's 12th birthday, today, but it feels like every year.
She has grown so much in so many ways, but at the same time, there are things about her that are exactly the same.
I'm sure this is true for other mothers of kids who are around the same age as mine; my daughter has become a confident and kind lady.
She has her own set of friends, and her own personality, and now she is the one telling me my birthday stories instead of me remembering them.
And she has already started to think of me as the "old me".
In the past 3 years, I have been living my own life, but I have also watched her become a young woman.
There were times where I was proud of her, and times when I was scared for her.
She has her moments, just like any kid does, or any adult does, but she has always been a good kid.
She's always been kind to others, she's been honest, and always tried her best.
When I look back at our journey together, she has made me a better mother, and a better person.

sentences.sentence: Liz’s Bio and Featured Stories
If you like true stories with a twist and a life lesson takeaway, read on!
Photo Courtesy of the Author
Dear Reader,
Welcome to my little corner of the world!
I don’t often lay on the ground and tell you about myself, but today is an exception.
I am Liz.
To get to know me, let's start with what I do and how I became the person I am today.
First, who is Liz?
I live in the Pacific Northwest, a place where rain seems to be a permanent resident.
I’m a writer and a mom.
Being a writer for me started out as a dream that I didn’t think I could make come true.
Then, it turned into something that I never imagined.
Now, I’m writing a book, and every time I finish another chapter or edit one, I get to see how far I’ve come.
My other claim to fame is being a mom to my three children.
I can’t imagine a better job than this.
It takes a lot of sacrifice, but you end up with three amazing kids that will always love you.
Now, if you want to know why you’re reading about me, there is a reason.
That reason is the blog posts I have written here, which I call “Featured Stories.” I started this because it was the only thing that would fit the name and style that I had for my website.
However, once I got into it, I realized that this was where I wanted to go.
These are true stories that happen to me.
They are usually from my past, but they aren’t all happy.
These are life stories with a twist.
The twist is something that makes you say, “Oh, yeah, I know exactly how you feel.” And then there is the “Takeaway” at the end.
I think the purpose of these is to help others see things a little differently, because I did the same.

sentences.sentence: Illustration by Fresh Idea
Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the end of July.
I would have a lot of work to do, but it could be done.
I was excited.
I sat at my computer, typing away on the story that was just taking shape in my head.
But something strange happened.
I found myself getting upset with the characters I had created.
They didn’t know how to talk to each other, they didn’t act like themselves.
My ego got in the way, and suddenly I found my hands on the keyboard, doing anything but writing.
Instead, I was spending half of every day trying to get these characters to act the way I wanted them to.
This is what happens when we let our ego get in the way of our writing.
We can see something in the character and not be able to make it work, and this leads us to start changing it.
Or, maybe we just don’t like the idea the character came up with.
Whatever the reason, we start to change and it kills the flow of the story.
But this is so much harder than just letting it be.
The more you think about it, the more you have to go back and do research or ask yourself questions and then you wind up getting lost and having to go back and fix things.
And the more you mess around, the longer it takes.
I remember when I was editing my book, I spent more time changing my mind about what the character was going to say and do that I did on actually writing the book.
At one point, I spent three days deciding if a character should be wearing blue pants or red pants.
After all this time, I still couldn’t decide.
It felt like forever before I finally decided that I had wasted enough time, I would just pick blue pants.

sentences.sentence: How Prepared Are You for the Revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food, and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making it.
It was a world where everything made sense.
You had a location, you had a great menu, you worked hard, and things would be good.
But then it shook up.
First, there was the internet and social media, which started to change how we do business.
Then came some crazy new tech, like artificial intelligence, and some of us started to think – maybe we were looking at a new normal for the way the world does business.
I'm here to say that we’ve only just started to shake it up.
I’m going to give you my opinion on what in the world is shaking up the restaurant, food, and hospitality industry.
And let me tell you, if you aren’t ready to take this seriously, it’s time to get ready.
Because the shakeup isn't over yet.
In fact, we’re only a small way into it.
What I’m about to tell you might seem like something from a science fiction book, but it’s happening, and it’s about to hit our industry harder than you could possibly imagine.
First, we have the rise of the super computer, aka artificial intelligence.
I don’t mean to scare you, but it has already changed our world, and now it is making its way to the food service industry.
The question is, can we keep up?
Do we know what to do, or is there going to be a new world order where people are no longer needed to work at restaurants?
Is there a new world order we’re all supposed to prepare for, one with super computers, one with no jobs for people to do, and one with no need for anyone to make food anymore?
Now, don’t get me wrong.

sentences.sentence: The #1 Thing That Gets Me Through Difficult Days: My Coping Mechanism in Trying Times
I remember the first few hours after my mom took her last breath.
I had the feeling that I could never recover from what happened.
She was the glue that held me together for a long time.
I had been so close to her and she gave everything to me, yet now she wasn’t there for me.
It felt like the world around me had come to an end.
The days, weeks, and months that followed, I went through all kinds of emotions, but the one thing that got me through the hardest days was talking.
There is nothing more therapeutic than being able to let out your feelings with someone you trust.
Whether it's with a friend or a family member, they would listen and not judge because we can be in the same boat.
It makes you feel good when someone you care for cares back and is there for you.
The person doesn’t have to say much, just listen.
It’s not always easy to talk, especially if you have never done it before, but the second you open up and start talking, a weight is taken off your shoulders.
When I lost my mom, I spent those hours, days, weeks and even months talking.
My family and friends were here for me, but at the same time, they were going through their own difficult times.
They didn’t know how to react.
I understood that, but I was determined to get through this.
I kept talking until it finally became easier.
I am grateful for them to be able to hear me and to talk things out.
The hardest part is starting.
It gets easier as you keep talking.
You can talk to people you trust in real life or to yourself (I do both).
But don't be afraid to start.
If you can find someone, then you will see a difference in yourself, I promise.

sentences.sentence: Vision 2020: The Well
Recordings, talk notes, and application questions
Each week, we produce notes, discussion points, and application questions for the Sunday talks — helping you go deeper into everything we’re looking at together and resourcing our time with you.
Our goal is to make you think.
To get you talking.
And to help you make the ideas we study part of who you are.
The Bible says the first thing God created was not light.
It was a very dark and empty space, and in that dark, empty space, God created light.
God said let there be light, and there was light.
God called the light Day, and he called the darkness Night.
It didn’t have a name before then.
Then God took that light, which was the only thing named, and God made the waters so that they could separate from the land.
He made the sky to cover the water above, and he made the water to come together below, where he would put the land.
But the land wasn’t ready.
So God made the waters to rise and flood the earth and to cover it.
When the waters receded, God said the earth is now dry.
Then came the third day, and God created the dry land, with plants, trees, and fruit trees.

After that came the fish, the birds, the wild animals, and after all this, God said, “Let us make man.” He formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and man became a living being.

What I want to say today, though, is that the next words were, “It was good.” Not the land was good, not the sun and moon and the stars were good, not the plants and trees and the fish and birds were good.
The very first thing was light.
And after light, dry land.
But the second thing to be deemed good by God is the well.

sentences.sentence: Title: Don't I Know You?
As the fourth and final song faded, the DJ in our club at the north end of Waikiki kept the crowd pumped for another set of nude women on stage under the flashing black lights.
These men were mostly military dudes who were barely legal, and most of them were drunk.
They were all talking loudly, hitting on each other's girl friends and making a bunch of noise while waiting in the crowd for the next "show" to come out.
It was only when the "show" came out again that I realized that the man next to me looked very familiar; then it hit me.
It was one of my best college roommates, who I hadn't seen since we graduated in 2017.
He must have been at least 27 years old at this point, and he was one of the people I remember having a very good time with back in those days.
But something had really happened to him during the last year or so, because his hair was all over the place, and his clothes looked like he had been living out of a bag.

The last thing I could remember was his shirt buttoned up and being clean, neat, and well-dressed, but now he was wearing a T-shirt and short shorts, his face was red and he was sweating heavily, and he smelled like he hadn’t showered in three days.
I thought that if we ever saw each other, I would probably just say “Hi” and leave it at that.
But instead, as I watched his eyes move around the room, his mouth open and close, I realized that there might be some kind of opportunity to speak with him and find out why he had changed so much.
It was strange and it was a chance, so I decided to say hi to him, introduce myself, and see what happened.
He looked at me, and for a moment, he tried to remember who I was.

sentences.sentence: **Simple Changes That Helped Me Lose 5 Kg and Feel Great in Just One Month**
Image by biscotto87
When the pandemic-induced lockdown happened, I lost all motivation.
My lifestyle became sedentary.
Up until then, I had been taking care of my health in so many different ways that I could not figure out what was making me so unhealthy.
It took me some time to realize that it was all those small changes that had become one big change in the way I live.
I decided to go back to the basics.
So, for the last month, I tried simple things I never thought were so crucial to my health before.
Here is what made a difference:
1. **I started drinking at least 3 liters of water every day.
For a long time, I thought that I was drinking enough, but it turns out that if you drink only the 2 liters recommended by everyone, it is not enough.
Drinking more water can get rid of all those toxins, and it will keep your stomach feeling full and you won't have a desire for food as much.
2. **I stopped having coffee and milk.
This might sound silly, but the thing is that coffee and milk were my breakfasts and lunches for most of the time during the lockdown.
Having only a couple of glasses of milk a day was enough to make me gain weight.
I didn't know until I tried to stop.
3. **I started to walk for at least 20 minutes each morning.
Walking outside makes you feel great, and if you are walking in the park, or in a garden, you will find a lot of beauty to enjoy while you are doing something good for yourself.
4. **I started to do something that I like, that also keeps me active.
Before the pandemic, I used to be very active.

sentences.sentence: Photo by Harry Knight on Unsplash
"Card games, now that’s a good way to pass the time."
An older woman observes my group of fifteen high school students huddled in circles playing games.
We’ve just spent a week in the woods for our school’s survival training, and it’s our first free moment to kill some time.
I’m sitting in one of the circles, shuffling a deck of cards and preparing a game.
Most of the kids around me are staring blankly at their phones or tapping away on their computers.

An older woman observes my group of fifteen high school students huddled in circles playing games. We’ve just spent a week in the woods for our school’s survival training, and it’s our first free moment to kill some time. I’m sitting in one of the circles, shuffling a deck of cards and preparing a game.

Most of the kids around me are staring blankly at their phones or tapping away on their computers. “That’s how you get off the internet?” the lady asks sarcastically, “By getting on a deck of cards?”

When we got here, I thought maybe we would take the time to do what we were here for, which was to learn how to survive.

But no, we’re already glued to our phones. Maybe we’re all missing something if we can’t get off the internet and just live.
